summary.text: A 13-year-old boy was hospitalized in August 2015 with hoarseness and dyspnea for more than 20 days. He was diagnosed with hyperimmunoglobulin E syndrome and a T. marneffei infection, and nasopharyngolaryngoscopy revealed lesions of the pharyngeal and laryngeal regions. Table 1 lists cough, malnutrition, a skin lesion and lymphadenectasis as further manifestations, with ARDS as a complication.

The workup was negative for HIV and sputum culture indicated T. marneffei, with Candida albicans also listed as a confirmed pathogen. Whole-genome sequencing revealed a novel missense STAT3 mutation. Nasopharyngolaryngoscopy showed diffuse inflammation, purulent secretions, vocal cord edema, an unclear structure and narrowing of the glottic area. IgG, IgE and several lymphocyte subsets were reported above or below the stated normal range.

Mechanical ventilation was needed on two occasions because of ARDS and upper airway obstruction due to granulation tissue. Amphotericin B, voriconazole and imipenem-cilastatin sodium were given intravenously for 2 weeks and itraconazole orally for 2 months. P1 showed a good clinical response, although his glottic structures failed to recover completely after treatment.

summary.text: A 1-year-old boy was hospitalized in August 2019 with intermittent laryngeal stridor accompanied by a cough for more than 2 months, aggravated by hoarseness for 3 weeks. He was diagnosed with subglottic stenosis, and bronchoscopy showed injury to the glottic region. He had a T. marneffei infection with ARDS listed as a complication.

Whole-genome sequencing revealed STAT3 mutations, and the sputum culture indicated T. marneffei. Electronic bronchoscopy in 2019 showed an abnormal glottic structure with granulation tissue hyperplasia and inflammatory subglottic stenosis, a 2020 follow-up bronchoscopy showed obstruction from subglottic granulation tissue hyperplasia, and a laryngeal web was found in 2021.

Mechanical ventilation was required because of subglottic stenosis and acute respiratory failure, and voriconazole and itraconazole were administered as antifungal agents. P2 showed good clinical results and was discharged. Bronchoscopy after discharge showed that the glottic injury remained, and the glottic structures failed to recover completely after treatment.

summary.text: A 1-year-old girl presented in November 2021 with pharyngeal ulcers, a fever and a cough for 10 days. She was diagnosed with primary immunodeficiency disease and initially presented with ulcerative pharyngitis that subsequently progressed to nasopharyngeal adhesion. Table 1 also lists loss of weight, diarrhea, lymphadenectasis and hoarseness, with sepsis as a complication.

The workup was negative for HIV, the sputum culture indicated T. marneffei, and whole-genome sequencing revealed CARD9 mutations. In February 2022 nasopharyngolaryngoscopy diagnosed posterior nostril atresia, and posterior rhinoplasty surgery was performed. Nasopharyngolaryngoscopy after surgery showed significant hyperplasia of nasopharyngeal scar tissue.

Amphotericin B and itraconazole were required as antifungal agents. P3 showed good clinical results and was discharged. During follow-up, nasopharyngeal adhesion was observed and treated with surgery, and in 2023 nasopharyngolaryngoscopy showed rhinitis, adhesions and posterior nostril atresia. At the time of publication she had no cough or wheezing but was still breathing with an open mouth.

Nasopharyngolaryngoscopy in P3. Preoperative findings revealed posterior nostril atresia (a–c). The postoperative assessment following posterior rhinoplasty demonstrated hyperplasia of nasopharyngeal scar tissue (d–f). Additional observations at follow-up included rhinitis, nasopharyngeal adhesions, and posterior nostril atresia (g–i).

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the three JPEGs are inspected in the separate visual submission.

Table 2 results are scoped by the text sentence "The laboratory results ... at the time of admission are summarized in Table 2", so every resulted Table 2 cell carries that time with the scoping sentence as evidence; the N/A cells carry no time.
Table 2 cells reading N/A (P2 CRP and PCT) are recorded as not reported, because the source does not say the test was not performed.
Flags (high/low) only where the results paragraph states them; no flags were derived from the printed reference ranges.
Table 2 unit of Th/Ts is printed as % with ratio-like values; transcribed literally without correction.
Table 1 lists ARDS for P2 while the treatment paragraph names acute respiratory failure; recorded as separate conditions.
Statements that a treatment was needed or required (mechanical ventilation for P1 and P2, antifungal drugs for P3) are recorded with action unknown because administration is not stated.
The 10-day duration in the P3 presentation sentence may apply to the cough only; not attached to any single symptom.
Discussion statements about P3 surgery (nasopharyngeal surgery; glottic structure recovery) cannot be linked to a specific operation.
